title: Investigate p.settings-permission-status empty space

messages.content: What is p.settings-permission-status and why is it taking up empty space in settings?
messages.editable_content: What is p.settings-permission-status and why is it taking up empty space in settings?

messages.content:
`p.settings-permission-status` is the status message paragraph under the "Local Search" sources in the settings panel (`SettingsPanel.js:427-429`). It's created and appended to the DOM unconditionally for every user, but its `textContent` only ever gets set inside the checkbox's `change` handler (lines 444-467) — when the user toggles "Bookmarks" or "History" and a permission grant/denial result comes back, or on error. So on initial render (and any time the user hasn't touched those toggles this session), it's an empty `

`. That's why it "takes up empty space": the CSS gives it `min-height: 16px; margin: 4px 12px 0;` (meridian.css:1071-1077) specifically so the layout doesn't jump when the text appears/disappears — but that same reserved-height rule means an empty paragraph still occupies ~16px plus margin even with no visible text. So it's working as designed (a fixed-height placeholder for a status message that appears only after a permission-related toggle action), but if that reserved gap feels like wasted space when nothing's ever been toggled, options would be: only render/insert the `

` after the first status update, or drop `min-height` and accept a layout shift when text appears.

messages.content: Why in the world would I need a status message that "History access disabled" when I just unchecked it?
messages.editable_content: Why in the world would I need a status message that "History access disabled" when I just unchecked it?

messages.content:
Fair pushback — for the *disable* path specifically, it's pretty redundant. The message logic (SettingsPanel.js:454-458) is:

```js
permissionStatus.textContent = result.denied
  ? `${source.label} permission was not granted. This source remains off.`
  : `${source.label} access ${result.enabled ? "enabled" : "disabled"}.`;
```

That single branch has to cover three cases with one string: (1) you tried to *enable* and the browser granted it, (2) you tried to enable and the browser *denied* it, (3) you just unchecked it. Cases 1 and 2 genuinely need a message — the checkbox alone can't tell you "the OS/browser permission prompt was declined, so this stayed off," and it's `aria-live="polite"`, so screen-reader users get an announcement a checkbox state change alone wouldn't reliably give them.

But case 3 — you unchecking a box that doesn't need a permission grant to turn off — doesn't need any of that. Revoking is not async-fallible the way granting is (the `finally` just re-enables the checkbox), so "History access disabled" is telling you something the checkbox already told you, right next to it.

So it's not that the status paragraph is pointless — it's that the same code path fires it for both "meaningful permission result" and "trivial off-toggle," when really only the enable/deny case should populate it. A cleaner version would only set `textContent` when `requested === true` (i.e., only on enable attempts), leaving disable as a silent, self-evident checkbox flip.
In what case would the browser deny the permission?
messages.editable_content: In what case would the browser deny the permission?

messages.content:
That confirms it: `denied` only ever gets set on the *enable* path, via `chrome.permissions.request(...)`. So the "denial" case is specifically about Chrome's optional-permissions prompt for `bookmarks` / `history`:

- **User explicitly declines** the native Chrome permission popup ("Meridian wants to add the following permission: Read your browsing history" → user clicks *Deny*/cancels it). `chrome.permissions.request` resolves to `false`.
- **The request throws** (caught and treated as denied too, line 53-54) — e.g. the call isn't made in response to a genuine user gesture (Chrome requires `permissions.request` to originate from a direct user action, so if it's ever invoked programmatically outside a click handler, Chrome rejects it), or an invalid/unknown permission is requested.
- **Enterprise/managed policy** blocks the extension from acquiring that permission (admin-configured `ExtensionSettings` / blocked permissions list) — the prompt may not even appear and the call just resolves false.

So the "History permission was not granted" message exists for a real, meaningfully-different-from-a-checkbox event: the user (or their org policy) refused a native OS-level permission grant, and the UI needs to explain *why* the checkbox snapped back to unchecked even though the user clicked to turn it on. That's the one case in this function where the status text earns its keep — it's the *disable* branch (lines 57-63, permission removal) that never sets `denied` and doesn't need the status message at all.

messages.content:
Agreed — that fixes the actual complaint (empty reserved space) and drops the redundant success-message case in one move. Concretely that'd mean: - Only set `permissionStatus.textContent` when `result.denied` is true (or on the catch-block error) — drop the "access enabled/disabled" branch entirely. - Toggle a hidden/empty state on the `

` itself (e.g. add/remove a class, or just clear `textContent` and let CSS use `:empty { display: none }`) so it collapses instead of reserving `min-height: 16px` when there's nothing to say. Want me to make that change to `SettingsPanel.js` and `meridian.css`?

Yes. It's also very strange that they search bar's bookmarks/history buttons don't honor this. For example, turning bookmarks/history off should remove the bookmarks/history buttons. Currently, the buttons persist when the checkboxes are off and clicking them turns the checkboxes back on, which is strange behavior.

Done. Summary of changes (applied to both `components/`/`meridian.js`/`meridian.css` and the `meridian-extension/` mirror, which were kept in sync):

**1. Permission-status message** (`SettingsPanel.js`, `meridian.css`)
- `permissionStatus.textContent` is now only set on the `denied` case (or the catch-block error) — a plain enable/disable no longer writes redundant text.
- Dropped `min-height: 16px` and added `.settings-permission-status:empty { display: none; }`, so the paragraph collapses to nothing when there's no message instead of reserving space.

**2. Scope chips (bookmarks/history buttons) now honor the Settings toggles** (`meridian.js`, `components/sidebar.js`)
- Added `syncScopeButtons()` in both the new-tab page and the side panel: it reads `getEnabledLocalSearchSources()` and hides (`hidden` attr + `.hidden` class) whichever chip's source is off, running on init and whenever `localSearch` changes (via the `settings-changed` event in `meridian.js`, and `chrome.storage.onChanged` in `sidebar.js`).
- If the active scope's source gets disabled out from under it, it now falls back to `all` instead of staying pointed at a hidden chip.
- Click handlers no longer call `setLocalSearchSourceEnabled(..., true)` — since a chip is only ever visible when its source is already enabled, clicking it is now purely a scope-filter toggle, not a re-enrollment action. Removed the now-unused `setLocalSearchSourceEnabled` imports from both files.

Net effect: Settings is the single place that grants/revokes the permission; the search-bar chips are just a reflection of that state, and clicking a chip can no longer silently flip a checkbox back on in Settings.

messages.content: Do we have these open local search options on by default?
messages.editable_content: Do we have these open local search options on by default?

messages.content:
No — per `DEFAULT_LOCAL_SEARCH` in `utils/localSearch.js`:

```js
export const DEFAULT_LOCAL_SEARCH = {
  tabs: true,
  bookmarks: false,
  history: false,
};
```

- **Tabs** search is on by default (no special browser permission needed).
- **Bookmarks** and **History** are both off by default — they require the optional `bookmarks`/`history` Chrome permissions, so they only turn on when the user explicitly enables them via the Settings checkboxes (which triggers the `chrome.permissions.request` prompt).

Consistent with the chip behavior we just fixed: on a fresh install, the bookmarks/history scope chips in the search bar stay hidden until the user opts in through Settings.

messages.content: What is the default New Tab behavior?
messages.editable_content: What is the default New Tab behavior?

messages.content:
The default is **"Open a new Meridian tab"** (`id: "meridian-view"`).

- `getNewTabBehavior()` in `meridian.js` falls back to `"meridian-view"` when nothing's stored: `newTabBehavior ?? "meridian-view"`.
- The Settings panel's local variable defaults the same way (`let newTabBehavior = "meridian-view"`).

That's one of three options under **Settings → New Tab Behavior**:
1. **Open a new Meridian tab** (`meridian-view`) — default; every new tab just shows Meridian, no special handling.
2. **Return to the pinned Meridian tab** (`focus-pinned`) — if a Meridian tab is already pinned in the window, opening a new tab instead activates that tab and closes the fresh one.
3. **Open a specific page** (`open-homepage`) — redirects the new tab to a configured homepage URL instead.

softSummary:
Working on the Meridian browser extension (root files plus a synced `meridian-extension/` mirror). Investigated `p.settings-permission-status` in `SettingsPanel.js` (line ~427) — an empty `

` reserving `min-height: 16px` via `meridian.css` (~line 1071) even when no message was set. Traced its `textContent` logic (lines ~444-467) to a single branch covering enable-success, enable-denied, and disable cases; determined only the `denied`/error case is meaningful (denial comes from Chrome's optional-permissions prompt being declined, throwing outside a user gesture, or enterprise policy blocking it). User decided: only set text on denial/error, and collapse the paragraph via CSS `:empty { display: none }` instead of reserving space. Also fixed: search-bar bookmarks/history scope chips didn't respect Settings toggles — clicking a hidden-should-be chip silently re-enabled the permission checkbox. Added `syncScopeButtons()` in `meridian.js` and `components/sidebar.js` to hide chips for disabled sources (via `settings-changed` event / `chrome.storage.onChanged`), fall back active scope to `all` if hidden, and removed chip click handlers' now-unused `setLocalSearchSourceEnabled` calls/imports. All changes applied to both `components/SettingsPanel.js`/`sidebar.js`/`meridian.js`/`meridian.css` and the `meridian-extension/` mirror, kept in sync. Syntax sanity-checked. Next: manual verification in browser (toggling settings, checking chip visibility/behavior) not yet done.
